During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the source will be cloned, and the `pkgver()` function will execute to compute the version based on Git history. This function uses safe, built-in Git commands (`git rev-list --count HEAD` and `git rev-parse --short HEAD`) that do not introduce remote code execution or data exfiltration risks.

There are no top-level command substitutions, `curl`/`wget` calls, `eval`, `base64` decoding, or other suspicious operations outside of the `pkgver()` function. The `pkgver()` function itself only reads local Git metadata after the repository is cloned — a standard practice in `-git` packages. No network requests occur during sourcing beyond the initial `git clone` implied by the `source` array, and no sensitive data is sent out. The rest of the PKGBUILD (e.g., `build()` and `package()`) is irrelevant for this narrow gate since those functions are not executed under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`.

Thus, running the specified `makepkg` commands will safely fetch and parse the package without executing any malicious payloads or exfiltrating data.
</details>
